summary: Independently verified all four criteria, repository checks, and visual comparisons. No technical findings recorded.

acceptanceCriteria.probe: Ran npm run test:e2e -w @wx/web -- --grep 'three populated meters': 2 tests passed in Chromium and WebKit. Independently launched both engines against Vite with viewport 1024×714, blocked Google Fonts, and intercepted measures/history using the existing current-and-refreshed-readings.json fixture mapped to garden, living room, and bedroom. Asserted each card's name and populated temperature, three grid tracks, equal top coordinates, complete viewport containment, and scrollY=0. Both engines reported card tops at 100px, bottoms at 502.296875px, and approximately 304.7px-wide tracks. At 1023px the grid had two tracks. Rendered the approved HTML prototype at 1024×714 in both engines and compared screenshots: the intended three-column, single-row layout matches, with every meter fully visible. Inspected styles.css: min-width 1024px applies repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)). Ran npm run test:visual -w @wx/web, then npm run test:visual -w @wx/web -- --update-snapshots, then npm run test:visual -w @wx/web again: all six comparisons passed each time; regeneration left all six reference PNGs byte-identical.

Read packages/web/AGENTS.md and README.md; ran node --input-type=module with node:assert/strict to match /Tablet: 1024 × 714/ in AGENTS.md and /tablet \(1024 × 714\)/ in README.md. Both assertions passed.

Read ROADMAP.md; ran node --input-type=module with node:assert/strict to assert that the R-07 table row includes 1024×714, the detailed description includes '7-inch 1024×714 IPS LCD HDMI capacitive touchscreen', and no 1024×600 remains. All assertions passed.

Read packages/web/e2e/dashboard.visual.spec.ts; ran node --input-type=module with node:assert/strict to assert the exact entry { label: 'tablet', width: 1024, height: 714 }. Assertion passed. Both tablet visual tests also executed successfully in the pinned Linux Docker wrapper.
